facts: If $TA$ is a chord at the point of contact $T$, the tangent-chord angle equals $\angle TBA$ for any $B$ on the far arc.
steps: Identify the point of contact, the tangent, and the chord that forms the tangent-chord angle.
Identify the alternate segment — the arc on the far side of the chord from the tangent-chord angle.
Set the tangent-chord angle equal to the inscribed angle in the alternate segment, then solve.

workedExamples.solution_text:
$\angle PAB=72^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)
$\angle APY=46^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)

$\angle APB=62^{\circ}$

$\angle APB=\angle PBA$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle)
$\angle PBA=\frac{180^{\circ}-76^{\circ}}{2}$ (angle sum of a triangle)
$\angle PBA=52^{\circ}$
$\angle APY=52^{\circ}$ (alternate segment theorem)

$\angle OCB=90^{\circ}-x$ (a tangent is perpendicular to the radius at the point of contact)
$OC=OB$ (radii)
$\angle OBC=90^{\circ}-x$ (base angles of an isosceles triangle)
$\angle COB=180^{\circ}-2(90^{\circ}-x)$ (angle sum of a triangle)
$\angle COB=2x$
$\angle CAB=\frac{1}{2}\angle COB$ (angle at the centre is double the angle at the circumference standing on the same arc)
$\angle CAB=x$
$\therefore\angle BCQ=\angle CAB$

mastery.solution_text:
$\alpha + \beta = 90^{\circ}$ (tangent is perpendicular to the radius $OT$)
$\alpha = 90^{\circ} - \beta$
$OT = OA$ (equal radii), so $\triangle OTA$ is isosceles
$\angle OAT = \angle OTA = \beta$ (base angles of isosceles triangle)
$\angle TOA = 180^{\circ} - 2\beta$ (angle sum of $\triangle OTA$)
$x = \frac{1}{2}\angle TOA$ (angle at the centre is twice the angle at the circumference, standing on the minor arc $TA$)
$x = \frac{1}{2}(180^{\circ} - 2\beta) = 90^{\circ} - \beta$
$\therefore \alpha = x$
